page.overview:
What is Mynoghra?

Mynoghra, also known as The She-Daemon of the Shadows, is a fictional entity created by the late American author Edward P. Berglund for his 1975 short story "Wings in the Night".

Mynoghra is a cosmic entity capable of manifesting in a variety of forms, including that of a beautiful woman, but in its true form possesses a pair of membranous wings and is highly averse to any form of light. Despite this, Mynoghra has shown to be capable of extinguishing any light sources it encounters, and is usually surrounded by a cloud of inky blackness to protect herself from its effect in any case.

A Great Old One mentioned as a cousin of Nyarlathotep in The O' Khymer Revelations, and the Count de Hammais’ Sorcerie de Demonologie states that of all the Great Old Ones, Nyarlathotep and Mynoghra are the only ones not to be "imprisoned beneath the Elder Sign," and that once summoned, a portal to its dimension is created which may only be closed by the person who opened it.

Mynoghra likes to forge pacts with mortals for an unnamed price, although usually this price is the life-essence of the other party, as the entity finds this to be a particularly delicious repast. The remains of the victim are then fed to Mynoghra's Hell-Hounds, demonic entities only vaguely described but which bear some unspecified connection to the Hounds of Tindalos despite being the offspring of Mynoghra and Shub-Niggurath. In exchange, she may offer boons such as artistic inspiration; these pacts are always brought to a close on All Hallow's Eve. (: "Wings in the Night")
